description: Execute all three approved parts as one coherent, ordered edit to references/V6_TAG_DISCOVERY.md (primary) and references/V6_TAG_REFERENCE.md (reconciled). ORDER IS MANDATORY: capture everything FIRST (Part 1 additive inventory), THEN normalize grammar (Part 2) on top of the complete inventory, THEN group mode-specific techniques under labeled modes (Part 3). Never normalize-then-discard; nothing is deleted before it is documented. The user's #1 requirement is that no potentially-useful technique is omitted. This is a single feature because the three parts are tightly interdependent (Part 2 and Part 3 both reference the exact technique set introduced in Part 1) and must land together to leave the doc self-consistent.
steps: PART 1 (additive, lose nothing): Add a new section titled 'V6 Technique Inventory' to references/V6_TAG_DISCOVERY.md, placed AFTER the CONFIRMED FINDINGS section and its Context, and BEFORE (or replacing/superseding, see step for contradiction) the older 'Converged V6 Tag Format' passage. Catalog EVERY distinct technique observed. For EACH technique give: (a) a name, (b) a one-line description, (c) a minimal concrete bracket example, (d) a mode label (Default/Roots [folk, blues, mountain-gothic] vs. Concept-Album/Cinematic 'MODE C'). Split into COMMON (load-bearing spine) and RARE (at-risk) subsections.

PART 1 COMMON techniques (all 6, appear across all/most examples): 1) Full 13-part structural arc: Intro -> Verse -> Pre-Chorus -> Chorus -> Post-Chorus -> (Verse) -> Bridge -> Breakdown -> Build -> Drop -> Instrumental Solo -> Interlude -> Key Change -> Final Chorus -> Outro (identical across every example). 2) Instrument entrance/exit choreography (In/Out, Enter/Exit, Entrance, -in/-out) -- the confirmed-working V6 capability. 3) Dynamics as an explicit arc: pp/hush -> crescendo -> full/ff -> drop -> fade (both classical pp-ff markings AND named Crescendo/Swell/Drop). 4) Call-and-response with response on its own line: [Call] ... / [Response] ... (or Male/Female alternation). 5) Verse-1 -> Outro lyrical bookend (reprise opening image at end). 6) Stop-time / one-beat-silence right before the drop or final chorus.

PART 1 RARE techniques (all 10, most at risk -- MUST all be preserved): 7) Compound/bundled transition -- multiple simultaneous events in one tag: [Transition: Crescendo, Snare In, Synth Riser]. 8) Voice-as-instrument muting -- [Instrument: Male Lead Out] / [Vocal: Vocal Out] to drop the vocal out on cue. 9) Call-and-response used as NARRATIVE REVEAL -- responses accuse/answer the narrator (Haunted Chamber-Folk 'Who closed the window? / You did'); storytelling THROUGH tag structure. 10) AI-voice-as-second-character -- [Response: low-register AI voice], [Low AI Voice: Compliance is a form of memory.] (Fractured Shadows concept-album device; a distinct MODE, must NOT be flattened into generic 'harmony'). 11) Progressive signal/glitch degradation -- [glitch-density: low -> medium -> high], escalating GLITCH-CUT through the song (time-based automation, cyber material). 12) Spoken-word surveillance interludes -- clinical, telephone-filtered, calm invasive whisper second voice (Fractured Shadows 03/04); a whole delivery mode. 13) BPM change mid-song -- [Tempo Change: 72 to 60 BPM], [accelerando: 78 to 82 BPM] (actual tempo modulation, distinct from 'half-time feel'). 14) Panning / spatial cues -- (whispered thoughts) panning left-to-right; [whispered ad-lib, panned right] (stereo-field direction). 15) Key-change with the SPECIFIC modulation named -- A minor -> C major (relative-major comeback), D minor -> E-flat minor (up-a-semitone unease), Fm -> Ab; the interval carries meaning; reserved for emotional payoffs. 16) Em-dash for breath/phrasing within a line -- 'Another night -- another screen glow' (micro-level delivery control easily destroyed by cleanup).

PART 1 observations (record as observations in the inventory, NOT as endorsed practice): the examples exhibit SIX inconsistent tag grammars for the same concepts -- (a) namespaced [Instrument: Banjo In], (b) bare [Banjo In], (c) verbose [Instrument Entrance: ...], (d) compact-pipe [VOCABULARY:INSTRUMENTS=...], (e) per-line-prefixed [VERSE 1][GUITAR:ENTER] on every line, (f) ALL-CAPS [STRUCTURE:VERSE]. Flag two artifacts: several examples over-tag (15-25 tags on a 4-line verse, some lines all-tags-no-lyric); and examples #4/#5/#6 contain the ENTIRE song duplicated twice (copy/paste artifact, not intentional).

PART 2 (normalize grammar, on top of the complete inventory so nothing is lost): Add a 'Canonical V6 Tag Grammar' section defining ONE canonical bracket grammar, grounded in the confirmed findings + the best shipped song 'From the Floor to the Fire'. Rules: light-namespaced event tags [Instrument: Banjo In], [Vocal: Belt], [Dynamic: Crescendo]; [Role, inline-adjective] for vocal delivery [Female response, rising], [Male lead, tender then stronger] elevated to a first-class recommended form; NO [Tag Vocabulary] block in final output (confirmed); 2-4 tags per SECTION, not per line; no bar-level micro-tags ('enters on final two lines', 'sixteen-bar solo') in the lyrics field -- move those to Production Notes. CRITICAL: normalizing = standardizing HOW a technique is written, NOT removing WHICH techniques exist. Every technique from Part 1 must remain expressible in the canonical grammar -- show that they are.
PART 2 migration table: Provide a small 'grammar migration' table mapping each of the six observed dialects (a-f from the observations) -> the canonical form.

PART 3 (labeled modes): Restructure so mode-specific techniques are explicitly grouped under labeled modes rather than merged into a default. Define: (i) a Default/Roots mode (folk, blues, mountain-gothic) = common spine + folk-leaning techniques; (ii) a Concept-Album/Cinematic mode, using the user's established label 'MODE C (Cinematic/Theatrical/Concept)', where AI-voice-as-second-character (#10), progressive glitch degradation (#11), and spoken-word surveillance interludes (#12) live as EXPECTED, mode-specific tools -- flagged as belonging to that mode, not the folk default. Make explicit that both modes SHARE the common spine (Part 1 items 1-6) but diverge in mode-specific techniques.

CONTRADICTION RESOLUTION: The doc currently both recommends dropping the [Tag Vocabulary] block (CONFIRMED FINDINGS #1 / RESULTS LOG) AND presents it as recommended in the older 'Converged V6 Tag Format' passage (part 1 of that section). Resolve to the confirmed 'drop it' stance: revise/annotate the 'Converged V6 Tag Format' passage so the [Tag Vocabulary] block is clearly labeled an EARLY EXPERIMENT that is NOT recommended for final output, with a pointer to the canonical grammar. Do not leave both stances presented as current recommendations.

PRESERVATION: Do NOT gut the existing 'working model' framing, the RESULTS LOG table, the 'Resolved / Working Model' list, or the 'Still Open' list -- extend them if needed but keep them. Keep the division-of-labor rule (Style = WHAT/identity, inline = HOW/arrangement) intact and consistent with all new content. Link to references/STYLE_LIBRARY.md for prose style prompts; do NOT duplicate its content.

RECONCILE V6_TAG_REFERENCE.md: Update references/V6_TAG_REFERENCE.md so its syntax guidance matches the canonical grammar defined in Part 2. Specifically: keep the master de-duplicated tag dictionary, but make the 'Tag Syntax Forms Observed' section and the 'Minimal V6 Song Skeleton' reflect the canonical forms (light-namespaced event tags; [Role, inline-adjective] delivery form as first-class; 2-4 tags per section; no [Tag Vocabulary] block; no per-line/ALL-CAPS/pipe dialects presented as recommended). Add a short cross-link to the Technique Inventory + Canonical Grammar sections in V6_TAG_DISCOVERY.md. Do not delete the tag dictionary content itself.

Do NOT run tools/validate-song.py. Do NOT push or open a PR. Leave all changes staged/committed on the current branch per orchestrator instructions (the orchestrator handles commit/branch reporting; you may leave the working tree with the edits in place).
